extracted_concepts.name: Sample Space
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Set Ω of all possible outcomes.

extracted_concepts.name: Event
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Subset of the sample space Ω.

extracted_concepts.name: Classical Probability Model
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: P(A)=|A|/|Ω| when outcomes are equally likely.

extracted_concepts.name: Bayes' Theorem
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Updates P(A_j|B) using likelihoods and priors.

extracted_concepts.name: Binomial Distribution
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Number of successes in n independent trials.

extracted_concepts.name: Continuous Distribution
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Distribution described by a density f(x).

extracted_concepts.name: Marginal Distribution
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Distribution of one variable obtained from the joint distribution.

extracted_concepts.name: Convolution
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Integral formula for the distribution of X+Y.

extracted_concepts.name: Law of Large Numbers
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Sample mean converges to population mean.

extracted_concepts.name: Central Limit Theorem
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Standardized sums converge to a normal distribution.

extracted_concepts.name: Chi-square Distribution
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Distribution of sums of squared normal variables.

extracted_concepts.name: t Distribution
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Distribution used when variance is unknown.

extracted_concepts.name: Point Estimation
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Uses sample statistics to estimate population parameters.

extracted_concepts.name: Confidence Interval
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Interval estimate with specified coverage probability.

extracted_concepts.name: Hypothesis Testing
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Decides between H₀ and H₁ using a test statistic.

extracted_concepts.name: Z-test
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Normal-based test when σ is known.

extracted_concepts.name: t-test
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Test using the t statistic when σ is unknown.

extracted_relations.evidence: Events are subsets of Ω.
The axioms assign probabilities to events.
P(B|A)=P(AB)/P(A) uses probability axioms.
Bayes' theorem is written with conditional probabilities.
Independence can be expressed as P(B|A)=P(B).
X maps outcomes in Ω to real numbers.
A PMF specifies a discrete distribution.
The binomial distribution is a discrete distribution.
A PDF specifies a continuous distribution.
F(x)=∫₋∞ˣf(t)dt represents continuous probabilities.
The normal distribution is a continuous distribution.
A joint distribution describes two random variables.
Marginals are obtained by integrating the joint distribution.
Independence is defined by factorization of the joint density.
The sum formula f_Z(z)=∫f(x,z-x)dx uses joint structure.
Expectation is defined for a random variable.
Var(X)=E[(X-μ)²].
Cov(X,Y)=E(XY)-E(X)E(Y).
ρ standardizes covariance.
LLN states convergence of X̄.
The CLT limit is N(0,1).
X̄ estimates the population mean μ.
S² estimates the population variance.
(n-1)S²/σ² follows χ²(n-1).
The t-test uses the t distribution.
P(A)=|A|/|Ω| counts outcomes in Ω.
Point estimators are sample statistics such as X̄.
MLE is a point estimation method.
Normal-mean intervals are centered at X̄.
The Z-test is a hypothesis test.
